The throw statement acts as a precondition check to ensure the method receives a valid non-null argument. In Java, such preconditions are typically used to catch programming errors early, and the caller is expected to ensure the argument is never null. The exception is not intended to be caught and handled in normal control flow; rather, it signals a bug in the caller code.
